requirement:
The coverage workflow returns a failing exit status when test execution or
coverage collection fails and reports the failure.
Collecting coverage does not turn a failing test run into a successful command.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.test-coverage.failures`. I did not read any implementation source. The requirement has three obligations: a failing exit status when test execution fails, a failing exit status when coverage collection fails, and reporting the failure. A failing test run must also not become a successful command.

**Test execution fails, so the command fails and the failure is reported.**
- `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[real_parallel_processes_retries_child_profiles_and_filtered_reruns]` runs the `retries` test with `--retries 0`, so the test really fails.
  - It asserts that the command status is not success.
  - It asserts that the saved run's `outcome` is `"failed"` and that the failed attempt's `outcome` is `"failed"`.
  - A later run that succeeds replaces the failure, which shows the failure was recorded as a distinct state.
  - In this test the failure is reported only through the saved run and attempt records. It does not assert on stderr text. I accept that as reporting, because the exit status and the recorded outcome both carry the failure and the test failure itself is shown by nextest.
- The same test also covers a build failure. A deliberate `compile_error!` makes the command exit non-success and leaves the saved set unchanged.
- This is the "failing test run is not turned successful" case. The exit status is non-success even though coverage collection has retained profiles.

**Coverage collection fails, so the command fails and the failure is reported.**
- `fn[passing_tests_with_missing_or_corrupt_profiles_fail_collection_and_retain_partial_reports]`:
  - The tests all pass, but one writes no profile and one writes a corrupt profile.
  - The test asserts a non-success exit status from both the direct `coverage` command and the full flow.
  - It asserts that stderr contains "partial profiles and reports have been retained".
  - It asserts that the saved run's outcome is `failed` and that the per-attempt diagnostics name the missing or corrupt profile.
  - It also asserts that the full flow prints no "Coverage check" output.
  - This is the strongest test of the "collection fails even though execution succeeded" case.
- `fn[a_process_that_cannot_start_is_failed_with_retained_attempt_metadata]` asserts a non-success status, a `failed` attempt, and the diagnostic "Cannot start test process".
- `fn[unreadable_build_inputs_fail_preparation_before_any_tests_start]` asserts a non-success status, stderr "Coverage preparation failed", and an unchanged saved set.
- `fn[a_build_that_cannot_start_preserves_the_current_set]` asserts a non-success status and that no new set is created.
- `fn[cleanup_failure_is_reported_and_next_collection_removes_orphans]` asserts a non-success status and stderr containing "Permission denied".
- `fn[execution_startup_failure_leaves_prior_selected_results_pending_without_measurements]` asserts a non-success status and a saved run with outcome `failed` and a "No such file" diagnostic. It also asserts that the later saved check fails.
- `fn[a_failed_replacement_commit_reports_the_error_without_launching_execution]` asserts a non-success status and stderr containing "synthetic commit failure".
- `fn[interrupting_the_parent_preserves_started_attempt_metadata]` asserts exit code 130, outcome `interrupted`, and that the saved check fails.

**Verdict.** Every failure mode I derive from the requirement has a test that exercises it. Each test asserts a non-success exit status and a visible report, either stderr text or a recorded failed outcome and diagnostic. The failing-test scenario itself is checked mainly through the exit status and the recorded outcome, which I consider sufficient.
